summary: Harbour light at Garnish on the Burin Peninsula: a beacon from 1874, its historic wooden tower renovated on the quay, and a quick red light still shown.

structures.type: square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery
structures.note: Historic tower, inactive since 1991 (Rowlett). Rowlett gives 6 m (20 ft) and dates the tower 1885; LighthouseFriends dates the beacon to 1874, moved to the breakwater in 1877, with an 1885 bedroom added at the tower base. The record's 3.0 m (Wikidata) has no cited source.

structures.type: square skeleton tower, red and white rectangular daymark
structures.note: Working light: structure 4.3 m above ground (CCG list). In service from 1991, when a modern skeletal tower replaced the historic tower's function (LF). Rowlett gives 3.5 m (12 ft).

staffing.status: automated after electrification in 1967; caretaker of the automated light until 1991 (LF)

access.note: Historic tower on the quay: grounds open, tower closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). The working light is owned by the Canadian Coast Guard (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Garnish Heritage Society (historic tower site); Canadian Coast Guard (working light)

events.note: Beacon established by local people (LF); the Board of Works paid for labour on the Garnish Beacon in 1874 (JHA 1875).
George T. R. Snelgrove employed as the first keeper at $48 a year (LF); named as keeper in the Board of Works account (JHA 1875).
Tower moved to a new block at the end of the breakwater (LF).
Fire in the lantern room destroyed the lamp and lens; the tower caught fire and was quickly doused (LF).
Bedroom added at the base of the tower for the keeper (LF). The Lighthouse Directory dates the tower itself to 1885.
New lantern; signature changed to occulting white, five seconds on and five off (LF).
Light electrified; the Reeves family's keeping of the light ended (LF).
Historic tower light inactive (Rowlett); LighthouseFriends: its function was replaced by a modern skeletal tower.
Modern skeletal tower took over the light's function (LF).

corrections.why: 1991 is the year a modern skeletal light took over from the historic tower. The station's light was first shown as a beacon in 1874 (Board of Works account for Fortune Bay, JHA 1875 p. 145; LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: federal (working light); historic tower sold to the Town of Garnish for $1 and maintained by the Garnish Heritage Society
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse and that the historic tower was sold to the town. The Heritage Society maintains it. 'Nonprofit' describes the maintainer, not the owner.

The Lighthouse Directory gives 6 m (20 ft) for the historic square pyramidal tower. The record's 3.0 m is a Wikidata figure without a cited source. Proposed for editor review; the CCG list gives 4.3 m for the working light, a different structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Lighthouse Directory dates the historic tower to 1885. LighthouseFriends dates the beacon to 1874 (labour on the Garnish Beacon is in the 1874 Board of Works account, JHA 1875 p. 145), the move to the breakwater to 1877, and 1885 to a bedroom added at the tower's base. The record's 1885 'built' is therefore the Directory's date for the tower, not the start of the light.

The historic tower has been inactive since 1991 (Directory; LighthouseFriends). The working light still shows: the Coast Guard list gives a quick-flashing red light (Q R 1s), 8.5 m focal height and 6 nm range. The Directory gives a red flash every 3 seconds on a 3.5 m skeletal tower; the Coast Guard list is followed here.
The Coast Guard list gives the structure's height above ground as 4.3 m; the Directory gives 3.5 m (12 ft). The Coast Guard figure is used.

notes_for_editor: The 1874 beacon is confirmed by a Board of Works account (JHA 1875 p. 145, 'Labor,Garnish Beacon', $20.00; checked on the page image) and the keeper's account (p. 128, checked on the image: 'George T. R. Snelgrove, Keeper, 12 months' salary' $48.00, total $118.35). The 1879 estimate of $150 is on printed p. 16, 'Estimated Expenditure' under General Light Houses for the Year 1879 (checked on the image; the heading is OCR damaged). The story now says 'allows $150', not 'carry'. LighthouseFriends' inspector remarks (1875 'more useful' on the breakwater, 1879 tampering) and the 1880 fire rest on LighthouseFriends alone; I searched the 1875 and 1879 volumes for the inspector's words and did not find them, so those stay LighthouseFriends claims. Garnish's 1874 keeper account was read from the page image (the OCR's '13 mouths' is '12 months' and the total is $118.35); the story uses the $48.00 salary and the $118.35 total. The 'Fisheries' entry for 1874 names G. T. R. Snelgrove as salmon warden without a place; the story does not treat that as the Garnish man beyond LighthouseFriends' 1872 statement. The Garnish Heritage Society and the Town of Garnish history page were not reachable (townofgarnish.ca 404 at guessed URLs; the home page names a 'History of the Garnish Lighthouse' page not found). LighthouseFriends' visitor note says the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse, while its history says the historic tower went to the town; not resolved. Not used: the Lighthouse Digest database entry, a MapQuest aggregator, and lighthouses.wiki. Bertram Marsh is named as LighthouseFriends names him (caretaker until 1991). The Journal of the House of Assembly volumes for 1901-1903 returned HTTP 500 from dai.mun.ca, so the Keppel 1901 build is not checked in a primary source.
